name: Desmopressin Nocturia Studies
question: Does dose-titrated oral desmopressin reduce nocturnal voiding compared with placebo in adults with nocturia and excess nocturnal urine production?

design.population: Men aged at least 18 years with at least two nightly voids, nocturnal urine production exceeding functional bladder capacity, and a response during desmopressin dose titration.
design.description: Multinational, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III randomized trial
design.locator: Mattiasson 2002, PDF pp856-858, Figure 1 and Table 1

verdictNote: Efficacy applies to men who responded during open-label dose titration.
takeaway: Among desmopressin-responsive men with nocturia, three weeks of oral desmopressin produced a greater than 50% reduction in nightly voids in 28/83 (34%) versus 2/63 (3%) given placebo; hyponatremia occurred during preceding dose titration.

reports.label: Men's randomized trial
reports.citation: Mattiasson A, Abrams P, Van Kerrebroeck P, et al. Efficacy of desmopressin in the treatment of nocturia: a double-blind placebo-controlled study in men. *BJU Int.* 2002;89(9):855-862.
reports.followUp: 3-week double-blind treatment after dose titration and a 1-week washout

results.measure: Responder proportion after 3 weeks, intention-to-treat efficacy population
results.note: 151 randomized; 5 lacked efficacy data, leaving 146 in the intention-to-treat efficacy analysis.

results.measure: Between-group mean difference in change in nightly voids after 3 weeks
results.note: Means are baseline to end of double-blind treatment; difference is in change, not final means.

results.measure: Between-group mean difference in change in hours until first nocturnal void after 3 weeks
results.note: Means are baseline to end of double-blind treatment.

harms.label: Any adverse event during double-blind treatment
harms.note: Safety denominators are all randomized patients who took treatment.

harms.label: Serum sodium below 130 mmol/L during open-label titration
harms.note: All cases occurred before randomization; six were reported as hyponatremia and three led to withdrawal.

delivery.label: Dose titration and randomization
delivery.value: 224 entered oral desmopressin titration at 0.1, 0.2, or 0.4 mg at bedtime; 151 responders entered double-blind randomization after a 1-week washout.
delivery.locator: PDF pp856-858, Figure 1 and patient disposition

delivery.label: Fluid instructions
delivery.value: From 1 hour before bedtime until 8 hours after dosing, patients drank only to satisfy thirst and avoided diuretic drinks.

reports.label: Parallel women's randomized trial
reports.citation: Lose G, Lalos O, Freeman RM, et al. Efficacy of desmopressin (Minirin) in the treatment of nocturia: a double-blind placebo-controlled study in women. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2003;189(4):1106-1113.
reports.followUp: 3-week double-blind treatment after 3-week titration and 1-week washout

results.endpoint: At least 50% reduction in nightly voids
results.measure: Responder proportion after 3 weeks in a separate randomized cohort of women
results.note: The abstract does not state the prespecified endpoint hierarchy or alpha.

harms.label: Hyponatremia during open-label dose titration
harms.note: The abstract does not give the titration denominator or randomized-arm hyponatremia rates.

harms.label: Deaths during the women’s study (n = 2)
harms.note: Neither death could be directly associated with study drug; allocation and timing were not stated.

delivery.label: Dose titration and randomization
delivery.value: Women received 0.1, 0.2, or 0.4 mg oral desmopressin during titration; 144 responders were randomized equally to desmopressin or placebo.
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Study Design and Results

reports.label: Open-label long-term extension
reports.citation: Lose G, Mattiasson A, Walter S, et al. Clinical experiences with desmopressin for long-term treatment of nocturia. *J Urol.* 2004;172(3):1021-1025.
reports.followUp: 10 or 12 months of treatment, then 1 month off treatment
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methodology and Results, pp 1021-1022

results.measure: Mean nightly voids during 10 or 12 months of treatment versus pretreatment baseline, among patients assessed
results.note: Open-label extension of prior responders; descriptive safety-population analysis without a formal statistical test.

results.measure: Mean minutes from pretreatment baseline to 12 months, among patients assessed

values.exp: Men: 157 to 288 min; women: 142 to 310 min

results.note: First sleep period shortened during the month after treatment cessation; no formal statistical test.

results.endpoint: At least 50% reduction in nightly voids
results.measure: Responder proportion at 10 months among patients assessed, versus pretreatment baseline
results.note: Sex-specific denominators are assessed patients at 10 months; no formal statistical test.

harms.label: Withdrawal due to adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 1022, Table 1; p 1024, Table 4
harms.note: Thirty of 249 (12%) withdrew because of adverse events during long-term treatment.

harms.label: Serious drug-related adverse events
harms.note: Four men had six serious events considered drug-related. One woman had hyponatremia, headache and nausea; her vertigo was marked not related.

harms.label: Any and serious adverse events during long-term treatment
harms.note: One man died of renal carcinoma; death was not treatment-related.

harms.label: Hyponatremia during long-term treatment
harms.note: 33/35 were asymptomatic with sodium at least 130 mmol/L; one man and one woman had symptomatic class I hyponatremia (125 to below 130 mmol/L); none had class II (below 125 mmol/L).

harms.label: Treatment-related urinary tract infection
harms.note: Table 3 lists two events in the one affected man and three events in the three affected women.

delivery.label: Extension enrollment and completion
delivery.value: 132/143 men (92%) and 117/141 women (83%) who completed the short-term studies entered the extension; 95/132 men (72%) and 87/117 women (74%) completed 10 or 12 months of oral desmopressin 0.1, 0.2, or 0.4 mg at bedtime.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methodology, p 1021; Results, p 1022, Table 1

delivery.label: Treatment adherence
delivery.value: 115/132 men (87%) and 100/117 women (85%) ingested at least 80% of study medication.
